_comment: WHEN should a post be live, derived rather than decided. Replaces the fixed biweekly cadence killed 2026-10-10 at Will's direction: 'Your job is to be figuring out what topics need to be publishing based on what season we're in and how far ahead of dates that people usually book. Then schedule accordingly. Not just a static set-and-forget schedule.' Every lead time here has a source. Anything unsourced is marked unverified and says what would settle it.
owner: blog-editor agent; changes to the RULE belong to a session with Will

rule.clamp: Never later than seasonStart. If the derived date is already past, publish as soon as the draft is clean, because a late post still earns the tail of its own season and banks authority for the next one.
rule.whyRunway: A pin cannot precede its destination post, and Pinterest's own creator guidance is to place seasonal content 45 days before the event (45 to 60 is the common range). So the post has to exist before the pin, which has to exist before the search peak.
rule.whyNotWeekday: Publish weekday is close to irrelevant for search. Only 1.74% of new pages reach Google's top 10 within a year and 3 to 6 months is typical to rank at all, so the original 'Wednesday gives Google 24 to 48 hours to index before Thursday planning' reasoning confused indexing with ranking. Pick any morning; the post only has to be live before its pins fire.
rule.gapFiller: Evergreen posts (place stories, culture, property pieces) have no season and exist to fill the gaps the seasonal dates leave. Uneven gaps are correct output, not a bug to smooth.

offSeason.note: Nov to early Dec and late Jan to Feb. Sources give 2 to 3 months.

shoulder.note: May, Sep, Oct. Sources give 2 to 4 months.

peakSummer.note: Compressed from 34 days to 29 in recent data for the booking itself, but planning starts earlier; 60 to 90 is the advance-booking guidance.

holidays.note: Thanksgiving 2 to 4 months, Christmas 3 to 5 months, New Year 2 to 3 months.

propertySpecific.source: Airbnb Performance > Conversion > Booking lead time, listing 39025485, read from the host dashboard 2026-10-10
propertySpecific.supersedes: The 38.5 recorded in content/metrics/airbnb-metrics.json on 2026-05-15. That file is now stale by 18 days of lead time.

observedByPeriod.Nov-Dec stays: about 90, the highest of the year

propertySpecific.readingCaution: Read off the dashboard chart by eye, so treat these as approximate. The axis does not make clear whether a point is the stay month or the booking month, and the near-zero months are the months with almost no revenue, so their 'lead' is computed from a handful of last-minute bookings and carries almost no signal.
propertySpecific.WARNING: Still do NOT plan against 56.4. It is a realised average across all bookings and is dragged down by last-minute ones, exactly as 38.5 was. Plan against the HIGH end of a season's observed lead, because the job is to be live before the EARLIEST planners arrive, not the average one. A post live at the average lead has already missed half its demand.

bookingLeadResearch.propertyValidatesTheModel: The property's own observed peaks (about 90 for Nov-Dec, about 85 for Jun-Jul) sit at or just below the industry lead times this model already uses (90 off-season, 120 shoulder, 150 holidays). So the model is conservative in the right direction and the property data confirms rather than overturns it. The lead times below are therefore UNCHANGED on 2026-10-10. Lowering them to match the realised average would mean publishing later, which is the direction that caused the original problem.

whyOffSeasonFirst.finding: CORRECTED 2026-10-10 once monthly data back to 2023 arrived. 84% of the 2024-to-2025 decline was SUMMER, not the off-season: July fell $4,462 and August fell $5,812. The earlier reading, that the off-season was the main cause, came from seeing only 2025 and 2026.
whyOffSeasonFirst.august: August is the one month that never recovered: $6,898 (2023), $7,749 (2024), $1,937 (2025), $2,546 (2026). July and September both came back in 2026. About $5,200 a year sits in that one month and the cause is UNVERIFIED.
whyOffSeasonFirst.offSeason: Still real, still worsening, and still second: Jan-May fell from $15,652 in 2025 to $11,168 in 2026. December has gone $3,151, $476, $0 across three years.
whyOffSeasonFirst.consequence: Peak topics are NOT deprioritised as heavily as this model first said. summer-families stays low priority for June, July and September, which have recovered on their own. But AUGUST is a hole in the best season and content aimed at late-summer availability is now worth writing.

seasons.label: Winter cozy: sauna, hot tub, fire pit
seasons.segment: Couples and small groups, DC and Richmond drive market, looking for a quiet off-season weekend
seasons.why: The single biggest revenue gap. December 2025 earned $0 and Jan and Feb 2026 came in at $681 and $737. The sauna and hot tub are the only amenities that are actively better in the cold, so this is the property's strongest off-season argument and it has never been published into its booking window.

seasons.label: Winter birding and waterfowl
seasons.segment: Birders and slow-travel solo or couple guests, shoulder of the quiet season
seasons.why: Same booking window as winter-cozy and a different search intent, so the two do not cannibalise. Niche, low-competition keywords.
seasons.unverified: Peak waterfowl concentration dates on the lower Potomac are taken from the existing winter-birding draft rather than from a primary source. Settle with Virginia DWR or the Rappahannock River Valley NWR seasonal counts before leaning harder on this season.

seasons.label: Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year
seasons.segment: Multi-generational family groups, the one off-season window that fills a 4-bedroom house
seasons.why: The longest lead times of any season, 3 to 5 months for Christmas, so this is the one that punishes lateness hardest. Larger properties also book further out: 6-bedroom homes average 83 days against 41 for a one-bedroom.

seasons.label: Osprey return and spring birding
seasons.why: Osprey season on the Chesapeake runs March into September, and the return is the moment with search intent behind it.

seasons.label: Spring striped bass
seasons.why: A hard regulatory date, which makes it the easiest season to schedule against correctly.
seasons.anchorSource: 4 VAC 20-252-100, Potomac River tributaries: May 16 to Jul 6 and Aug 21 to Dec 31. https://law.lis.virginia.gov/admincodefull/title4/agency20/chapter252/
seasons.note: HULL CREEK IS A POTOMAC TRIBUTARY, not Chesapeake Bay. It is a 6.5-mile tributary of the tidal Potomac. The Bay season (Oct 4 opening) does NOT apply here. Will corrected this on 2026-10-10 and he is right; an earlier draft of the schedule review had it wrong.

seasons.label: Summer on the water: crabbing, kayaks, swimming
seasons.segment: Families with children, the peak-season core
seasons.why: Re-ranked 2026-10-10. Was lowest priority on the reading that peak needed no help. June, July and September did recover in 2026 and still need nothing. AUGUST did not: it fell from $7,749 in 2024 to $1,937 in 2025 and only $2,546 in 2026, the largest single recoverable sum on the property at about $5,200 a year. Write for late-summer and August availability specifically, not for summer in general.
seasons.note: The August hole is the target here, not the season as a whole.

seasons.label: Fall: rockfish, cooler water, no crowds
seasons.segment: Anglers and couples wanting the shoulder quiet
seasons.why: The fall rockfish season opens 08-21 on Potomac tributaries, seven weeks before the Bay. A post aimed at it must be live in late March, which is counter-intuitive enough that it was missed by five months in 2026.

knownGaps: No season covers March to early May beyond spring-birding. Shoulder-season content for that window is thin.

Guest-segment definitions are inferred from the content calendar's target-reader notes and from the drive market, not from booking data. Airbnb reservation exports would replace inference with fact; requested in analysis/candy-point-decline-2026-10.md and still outstanding.
No season model survives contact with real occupancy data. Revisit once the Airbnb CSVs land.

WHY August broke is unknown. The earnings report carries no nights and no rates, so it cannot say whether August lost bookings or lost rate. The Airbnb reservations export is still required and is now the highest-value missing input.
